findings.rule: PAGE_AUTHORING_CONTRACT.md Part 2: Worked mechanisms under Study scope 'Git fundamentals (branch, merge, PR)'
findings.change: Insert worked mechanism explaining 3-way merge recursive base calculation and diff conflict mechanics
findings.full_drafted_text: In distributed environments, Git calculates the merge base using a Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) search across the Directed Acyclic Graph. When multiple common ancestors exist (criss-cross merge topologies), the default ort (Ostensibly Recursive's Twin) strategy constructs a virtual merge base by recursively merging the ambiguous ancestors before diffing against branch tips. Git evaluates chunk-level differences line-by-line; if branch A modifies lines 10–20 while branch B modifies lines 40–50 relative to the merge base, both hunks integrate cleanly without conflict markers. If both branches touch overlapping line ranges with conflicting edits, Git halts automatic integration, marks the index stage registers (stage 1: merge base, stage 2: target branch, stage 3: incoming branch), and inserts conflict demarcation markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) for manual architectural resolution.

findings.change: Insert worked mechanism for RFC 9457 Problem Details structured error response parsing
findings.full_drafted_text: To prevent ambiguous error recovery, modern enterprise cloud architectures standardize on RFC 9457 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs) and Google API Design error schemas. An RFC 9457 payload returns Content-Type: application/problem+json with standardized keys: type (a URI reference identifying the problem category), title (a short human-readable summary), status (the HTTP status code), detail (an explanation specific to this occurrence), and instance (a URI reference identifying the specific transaction resource). When paired with Google-style error details (e.g. ErrorInfo domain and metadata maps, QuotaFailure violation lists, and RetryInfo backoff delays), downstream automated clients distinguish transient infrastructure capacity exhaustion from unrecoverable validation rejections without fragile regex parsing of unstructured strings.
